column1: # The support matrix behind PLATFORMS.md and the book's platforms table: one row per platform
# (the second lowerer, IREE, is a row too), one column per rung of the ladder — the suite
# (`scripts/platform/check.sh`, tiers 0-2), then `lake run mnist`, `cifar`, `imagenette`,
# `imagenet`. The proofs rung is platform-free (CI runs it) and has no column.
# A cell is the record of the LAST run of that rung on that platform, in the shape
#     DATE · WHERE (TAG); anything more
# — the date, a markdown link to the run directory or runbook section, an optional short
# parenthetical tag right after the link, and after that markdown-only detail; `-` when the
# rung has not been run there, which is not a failure; `n/a: why` when it cannot be. The `suite`
# column may be `auto:<host>`, and is then filled from the newest runs/platform/*/manifest.json
# with that host (date, verdict, pass count, link). `plugin` is what the shim dlopens and
# `runbook` the page that sets it up; `env` is scripts/platform/env.sh's profile for the row.
# scripts/platform/platforms_md.py renders PLATFORMS.md (every cell, as markdown) and
# blueprint/src/figures/platforms.tex (per rung DATE (TAG), the link dropped; the runbooks as a
# line under the table); `--check` fails when either committed output is stale. A new platform
# is a row here, an arm in env.sh, an expected file and a deploy/<X>.md runbook; check.sh
# regenerates both outputs after each suite run.
